states the research question about referee bias by skin tone

spans.assertion: the study used Bayesian logistic regression to model a player's red-card record as a function of seven predictors, addressing the skin-tone-bias question
referee strictness and player aggression were important nuisance/control predictors
initial analysis found the skin tone predictor's 95% credible interval did not overlap zero and its inclusion was supported by the Bayes factor, seeming to reinforce the referee-bias hypothesis
closer inspection revealed the data were contaminated by seven players with disproportionately high red-card rates, and removing these outliers (0.3% of the data) eliminated the bias effect entirely

spans.assertion: after removing seven outliers, the Bayesian logistic regression model no longer showed evidence that referees give more red cards to darker-skinned players

spans.note: restates the two crowdstorm research questions

spans.assertion: the mean IAT score and mean explicit bias score were z-transformed before being used as predictors
the two raters' skin tone scores were z-transformed and then averaged into a single predictor
cases with unknown IAT score were excluded before proceeding
cases with unknown skin color were deliberately not excluded, since they still provide information on referee strictness
the initial analysis used a probit regression, but the final analysis switched to logistic regression so the effect could be reported as an odds ratio

the logistic regression modeled red-card probability as a function of seven predictors: player aggression, referee strictness, IAT score, explicit bias score, player skin tone (average of two raters' z-scores), IAT×skin-tone interaction, and explicit-bias×skin-tone interaction
league country was left out as a predictor because its effects would be accounted for by player aggression and referee strictness
other possible predictors, deemed superfluous or uninformative (e.g. player position), were not added to the regression
IAT and explicit bias score predictors were included specifically to keep the interaction terms interpretable

spans.note: notes the research questions map onto predictors 5, 6, 7

spans.assertion: player aggression and referee strictness were not directly available but were estimated from the data set
aggression and strictness are treated as important nuisance/control predictors needed for an appropriate bias assessment
for each player-referee dyad the logit of red-card probability was modeled as cards[i] ~ dbin(p[i],games[i]), logit(p[i]) as a function of seven predictors
referee strictness and player aggression were each modeled as group-level normal random effects: refEffect[k] ~ dnorm(0,precRef), playerEffect[j] ~ dnorm(mu0,precPlayer)
the precision parameter was assigned a dgamma(1,1) prior and mu0 was assigned a more informative dnorm(-2,1) prior
these somewhat informative priors were found not to affect the key comparisons of interest
the five remaining slope predictors (slpIAT, slpEbias, slpColor, slpColIATint, slpColEbiasint) were each assigned an independent standard normal prior
the first analysis used a wide uninformative prior (sd=1) and a second analysis used a more peaked prior (sd=0.2) to test robustness of the conclusions

spans.note: explains how the two research questions map to predictors 5 and 6/7

spans.assertion: importance of predictors 5, 6, 7 was quantified by comparing the full model to three simplified models (A excludes predictor 5, B excludes 6, C excludes 7), with the full model outperforming a simplified version counted as evidence for that predictor's inclusion
the full regression model was fit to the data using JAGS code provided on the OSF website
parameter estimates were gauged via posterior distribution plots summarized by mean and 95% credible interval, and three Bayes factors were computed comparing the full model to each simplified model
because the simplified models are nested in the full model, Bayes factors were computed using the Savage-Dickey density ratio (prior-to-posterior ordinate ratio at beta=0)
the full model was fit using JAGS MCMC with 10,000 iterations in a single chain
no burn-in was used because visual inspection showed fast convergence
the first analysis used relatively wide, uninformative priors N(0,sd=1) on the key predictors

spans.note: reference to accompanying html file AllPlayers.html

spans.assertion: the posterior for the skin tone predictor's effect was found substantially away from 0
the 95% credible interval was [0.037,0.159] and the Bayes factor for inclusion was a modest 4.6; a one-sided test would raise this to about 9
an odds ratio and its 95% credible interval (1.394 [1.135,1.714]) were derived for the skin tone effect to satisfy the crowdstorm project's requirements
for an average player/referee combination, each SD increase in standardized skin tone rating raised red-card probability by .00035 [.00013,.00059], a modest increase
Figure 2 confirms the impression that the skin tone effect, if present, is small
the posterior for the IAT×skin-tone interaction (predictor 6) was relatively close to zero with mass mostly negative
the 95% credible interval was [-0.131,0.049] and the Bayes factor against inclusion of predictor 6 was 15.0
an odds ratio and CI (0.806 [0.493,1.302]) were derived for the IAT×skin-tone interaction
the posterior for the explicit-bias×skin-tone interaction (predictor 7) was relatively close to zero with mass mostly positive
the 95% credible interval was [-0.051,0.125] and the Bayes factor against inclusion of predictor 7 was 15.2
an odds ratio and CI (1.316 [0.701,2.395]) were derived for the explicit-bias×skin-tone interaction
the first (wide-prior) analysis overall provided some evidence for skin tone bias and evidence against the importance of the implicit/explicit bias measures
the prior specification was done without much substantive knowledge and, after seeing the data, appeared possibly too wide
the authors decided to explore the robustness of their conclusions against a narrower prior
the prior distribution on the three crucial slopes was changed to N(0,sd=0.2) instead of N(0,sd=1)
with the narrower prior, parameter estimates were similar to the wide-prior results (skin tone CI [0.035,0.152]; IAT interaction CI [-0.122,0.051]; explicit-bias interaction CI [-0.051,0.118])
unlike parameter estimates, Bayes factor results were affected by the narrower prior: the BF for skin tone inclusion rose to 19.9 (about 39 one-sided)
the narrower prior decreased the Bayes factor support against including the two bias-measure interaction predictors, from about 15 to 3.4
inspection of Figure 2 suggested part of the skin-tone effect may be due to outlier players who disproportionately receive red cards; Figure 5 presents a histogram of red-card proportions
only seven of 2053 players had a red-card proportion greater than 5%
these seven players were deemed outliers and excluded from consideration in the later analysis
the players with a red-card rate above 5% were found not representative of the player population

spans.note: general methodological point that outliers can greatly affect infrequent, skewed-distribution results

spans.assertion: all seven players with a red-card rate above 5% were eliminated from subsequent analysis (0.3% of the data) to obtain a more robust and reliable bias estimate
after removing the seven outliers, Figure 6 suggests the red-card proportion is higher for light-skin-toned players than dark-skin-toned players
the analyses below confirm this visual impression from Figure 6

spans.assertion: analyses were re-run after excluding the outliers, using the broad N(0,1) prior
with outliers excluded, the posterior for the skin tone effect was now almost perfectly centered around 0
the 95% credible interval was [-0.077,0.050] and the Bayes factor for exclusion of the skin tone predictor was 28.3
an odds ratio and CI (0.956 [0.771,1.184]) were derived for the skin tone predictor after outlier exclusion
after excluding the seven outlying players, the skin tone bias effect was completely eliminated
after outlier removal, the posterior for the IAT×skin-tone interaction was relatively close to zero with mass mostly positive
the 95% credible interval was [-0.047,0.174] and the Bayes factor against inclusion of predictor 6 was 8.6
an odds ratio and CI (1.445 [0.777,2.564]) were derived for the IAT×skin-tone interaction after outlier removal
after outlier removal, the posterior for the explicit-bias×skin-tone interaction was relatively close to zero with mass mostly negative
the 95% credible interval was [-0.191,0.043] and the Bayes factor against inclusion of predictor 7 was 7.4
an odds ratio and CI (0.587 [0.263,1.351]) were derived for the explicit-bias×skin-tone interaction after outlier removal
a narrow-prior analysis of the outlier-excluded data set was omitted, due to time constraints and because the crowdstorm project does not center on Bayes factors
an influence-function analysis of whether outlying players had unequal impact on the results was suggested but not carried out
analyzing yellow cards instead of red cards was considered as potentially more informative about bias, but was not carried out
time constraints forced the authors to omit these additional analyses (influence functions, yellow cards)

spans.note: Difference between Initial and Final Approach heading

spans.assertion: the link function was changed from probit (initial approach) to logit (final approach) in order to summarize the effect as an odds ratio
the effects of a more peaked prior were explored in addition to the initial prior choice
eliminating the seven outliers was the final change from the initial to the final approach
future work should invest more time and expertise in specifying appropriate priors for the crucial predictors
priors were found not to matter much for parameter estimation but to affect the Bayes factor results
the authors are relatively certain the seven outliers need to be excluded to reach reliable conclusions

spans.note: authors remain reluctant to conclude there is no bias evidence
uncertainty about the likelihood is described as worrisome for any modeling attempt

spans.assertion: one particular choice of predictors was made, though the authors acknowledge other choices were possible

spans.note: even including all available predictors would not rule out other important control predictors affecting the results

spans.assertion: initial analyses using Bayesian logistic regression supported the conjecture that referees are slightly biased toward giving red cards to dark-skin-toned players, but after excluding seven outlying players this effect was eliminated entirely

spans.note: interprets the result as illustrating that extreme observations can distort inference for low-probability, skewed-distribution events

spans.assertion: the analysis process is presented as demonstrating a drawback of preregistration, since the presence/impact of outliers was difficult to foresee in advance
it is evident to the authors that the outliers needed to be removed, otherwise the model would have been seriously misspecified

spans.note: notes the document presents the analysis in the order it was conceived and conducted

spans.assertion: the impact of the outliers was discovered at the very last moment
it would be interesting to examine whether conclusions from alternative crowdstorm approaches are similarly affected by outlier removal, though this was not done here
